name: Dither
description: WebGL2 animated noise-wave background rendered as a pixelated dithered image, with pointer-driven erase, reveal or ripple effects, click ripples and an intro reveal.
contents: Container div with a single full-size WebGL canvas
Two shader passes: animated fractal noise field and an ordered dither or palette quantizer
behavior: Noise waves drift continuously unless disableAnimation is set
Pointer over the page leaves a fading trail that erases, reveals or ripples the pattern depending on mouseEffect
Clicking inside adds up to 4 expanding ripple rings when clickRipple is on
Pattern grows outward from the center on mount when intro is on
Rendering pauses when offscreen or the tab is hidden
With prefers-reduced-motion the animation, intro, pointer effects and ripples are turned off and a static frame is drawn
Canvas resizes with the container, device pixel ratio capped at 2
editableByProps: Wave colors, background color (or 'transparent') and an optional palette of up to 8 colors
Wave speed, frequency, amplitude, scale, contrast and brightness
Dither pattern, number of color levels and pixel size
Mouse interaction on or off, effect type (erase, reveal, ripple), radius, strength and trail length
Click ripple, intro reveal and animation on or off
Device pixel ratio, className and inline style

needsCodeEdit.change: Allow more trail points, ripples or palette colors

needsCodeEdit.where: MODES map and the threshold function in DITHER_FRAGMENT

needsCodeEdit.change: Limit pointer tracking to the component instead of the whole window
needsCodeEdit.where: window.addEventListener pointermove and pointerdown calls in the main useEffect

fixed: Requires WebGL2, renders nothing if unavailable
Root is relative with h-full w-full, so the parent must have a height or the canvas collapses to 1px
Pointer listeners are attached to window, so pointer effects respond anywhere on the page, not only over the container
Trail limited to 16 points, 4 simultaneous ripples, 8 palette colors
Canvas has aria-hidden and is purely decorative, put content above it with z-index
Responsive: sizes from the container with a resize observer, works on mobile, touch pointers act only while pressed or moving
